prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Cedar Falls Municipal Drinking Water Treatment Plant excludes distribution. Aliases: River Intake Pump Station=Ironwood; High Service Pump Header=Juniper; Coagulant Dosing Skid=Marigold; North Filter Gallery=Cobalt; Laboratory Sample Receiving Bench=Sparrow; Maintenance Planner=Quarry; Distribution Dispatcher=Falcon; SCADA Historian Server=Lantern.
Sources/items: Raw Water Screen Channel—Rake Torque Snapshot; Marigold—Alum Batch Ticket; Laboratory Technician—Sample Chain Slip; Sparrow—checked Jar Test Photograph Set; South Filter Gallery—Filter Run Exception Note; Clearwell Level Controller—verified Clearwell Diver Entry Permit; Juniper—Pump Bearing Vibration Clip; Chemical Supplier Driver—Chlorine Cylinder Seal Log; Chief Operator—verified Backwash Solids Manifest; Falcon—Pressure Zone Handoff Card after setpoint/alarm/work verification. Residuals Hauler participates. Sparrow receives custody-controlled samples, records distribution zone/location/time, reports analytical status for complaint interpretation. Lantern links distribution quality entries to operating periods using Sample Chain Slip; retains pressure/flow/pump/alarm/event records.
Intake requires permissives; loss stops/alarms; screen high-high requires field confirmation. Chief Operator authorizes Storm Intake Mode: intensified monitoring/sampling, capacity-aware pumping; Falcon avoids unnecessary zone changes except demand/storage/public safety. Duty Engineer approves adjustments and reviews persistent pressure complaints/alarms/model discrepancies. Marigold holds approved dose on unreliable indications; sustained changes require laboratory/online comparison. Filter recovery requires verified wash/turbidity/valves/flow; breakthrough requires exclusion/Chief Operator approval. Backwash Recovery Tank return requires settling/clarity/sampling. Maintenance requires approved isolation/windows/return evidence; Chlorine Residual Alarm pauses maintenance and coordinates hydraulic/quality responses.
Chief Operator classifies advisory/controlled/critical upsets, directs conservative pumping, closes recovery. Coordinate Chlorine Contact Basin, clearwell/storage/demand; check level before major adjustments. Cobalt reliable status precedes capacity claims. North Distribution Pressure Station monitors suction/discharge/availability/communications; South Distribution Pressure Station uses delayed low-pressure booster start. Automatic stations sequence within limits/report abnormalities; manual/local reasons/duration/contact recorded. Communication loss preserves last-confirmed mode pending verification. Field crews pre-notify major valve changes; Falcon coordinates flushing/exercising/isolation and reserve notices. Handoffs include disabled alarms/temporary limits/inspections/complaints; Quarry receives recurring-solids inspection notices.

New part:
S198: Control-room coordination with field crews is conducted by radio or phone using clear station names, valve identifiers, expected direction of pressure change, and confirmation when work is complete.
S199: Normal distribution operation is restored when pressure zones are stable, station alarms are cleared or assigned, field work is accounted for, and the Chief Operator has no remaining operating restrictions.
S200: The control system for the Cedar Falls Municipal Drinking Water Treatment Plant shall use role-based access control with named accounts for operators, engineering users, maintenance users, and read-only review users.
S201: Shared credentials are not acceptable for routine operation of the River Intake Pump Station, North Filter Gallery, South Filter Gallery, Coagulant Dosing Skid, Chlorine Contact Basin, Clearwell Level Controller, High Service Pump Header, North Distribution Pressure Station, or South Distribution Pressure Station.
S202: Operator privileges shall be limited to the actions needed to run assigned plant areas, and engineering privileges shall require separate approval before setpoints, control logic, alarm limits, or historian configuration are changed.
S203: Remote access to the control network shall require multi-factor authentication, encrypted connectivity, a recorded business reason, and approval by the Chief Operator or Duty Engineer.
S204: Quarry maintains the weekly access review for maintenance accounts and disables privileges after reassignment.
S205: The SCADA Historian Server shall be protected as a critical asset because it supports compliance review, alarm analysis, operational trending, and event reconstruction.
S206: The control network shall be segmented from administrative networks, and only documented pathways shall be allowed between the SCADA Historian Server, operator workstations, controllers, and approved support systems.
S207: Security patches, firmware updates, and antivirus changes shall be tested in a controlled manner before deployment to equipment that affects water production or distribution pressure.
S208: The Chief Operator owns alarm governance for process alarms, and the Duty Engineer supports alarm limit review when control changes or recurring nuisance alarms are identified.
S209: Alarm priorities shall reflect consequence, response time, operator action, and the risk of losing treatment, storage, or distribution capability.
S210: A Chlorine Residual Alarm shall remain configured as a high-priority condition when residual concentration indicates a potential treatment compliance or public health concern.
S211: Alarm shelving, suppression, and disabling shall require a documented reason, a time limit, and review at the end of the operating shift.
S212: Standing alarms shall be reviewed during each shift turnover so that unresolved equipment failures are not hidden by routine acknowledgement.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
